examples.en: I get motion sick when I ride a bus for a long time.
I got seasick on the boat yesterday.

examples.ko: 멀미하지 않으려면 출발 전에 약을 먹으세요.
examples.en: To avoid motion sickness, take medicine before you leave.
I seated the carsick child in the front seat.

examples.ko: 차에서 책을 읽으면 멀미할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I get carsick if I read in a car.
I felt sick on the mountain road, so I opened the window.

explain: '멀미가 나다', '멀미를 하다'처럼도 자주 말해요. 탈것 이름을 붙여 '차멀미', '배멀미', '비행기 멀미'라고 하고, 약은 '멀미약'이에요. 속이 울렁거린다는 느낌은 '속이 안 좋아요'로도 말해요.

phrases.en: I get motion sickness when I ride a bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: '멀미하다'와 같은 뜻이고 멀미 증상이 생길 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as the headword, often used when the symptoms start.

phrases.en: I get bad car sickness, so I sit in the front seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자동차를 탈 때 생기는 멀미를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the sickness felt while riding in a car.

phrases.en: I took motion sickness medicine before getting on the boat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멀미가 나지 않게 먹는 약을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Medicine you take to prevent motion sickness.

explain_en: People often say it as '멀미가 나다' or '멀미를 하다'. Attach the vehicle to name it: '차멀미' (carsickness), '배멀미' (seasickness), '비행기 멀미'. The medicine is '멀미약'. You can also describe the feeling as '속이 안 좋아요'.

examples.en: I get a stomachache when I drink cold milk.
The child has been suffering from a stomachache since yesterday.
My stomachache was bad, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 아침부터 배앓이 때문에 학교에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: I couldn't go to school because of a stomachache since morning.
What should I do if I get a stomachache on the trip?

examples.ko: 배앓이에는 따뜻한 물을 마시는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For a stomachache, it's good to drink warm water.

explain: '배탈'은 먹은 것 때문에 탈이 난 것을 말하고, '배앓이'는 배가 아픈 증상 자체를 말해요. 아이들이 배가 아플 때 특히 자주 들어요. '배앓이를 하다'처럼 '하다'와 함께 많이 써요. 병원에서는 '복통'이라는 말도 써요.

phrases.en: My stomachache has been bad since yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배가 많이 아플 때 '심하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with 심하다 when the stomachache is bad.

phrases.en: My stomach hurts after eating.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배앓이'보다 더 일상적인 말투로, 지금 아픈 느낌을 바로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday way to say your stomach hurts right now.

phrases.example: 배앓이에 좋은 차를 한 잔 마셨어요.
phrases.en: I drank a cup of tea that is good for stomachaches.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~에 좋은'과 함께 쓰면 배가 아플 때 도움이 되는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '~에 좋은', it refers to things that help with a stomachache.

explain_en: '배탈' refers to an upset stomach caused by something you ate, while '배앓이' is the pain in the belly itself. You often hear it when children have tummy aches, usually as '배앓이를 하다'. At the hospital the word '복통' is also used.

examples.en: My lower abdomen hurt, so I went to the hospital.
My lower belly has been sticking out lately, so I started exercising.

examples.ko: 아랫배에 힘을 주고 노래를 불러 보세요.
examples.en: Try singing while tightening your lower belly.

examples.ko: 아랫배를 따뜻하게 하면 도움이 될 거예요.
examples.en: Keeping your lower belly warm should help.
I felt better when I rubbed my lower belly with my hand.
My lower belly gets cold, so I often get stomachaches.

explain: 몸이 아플 때 '배가 아파요'보다 위치를 구체적으로 말하고 싶을 때 써요. 노래나 운동에서 '아랫배에 힘을 주다'라는 말을 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: When you sing, put strength in your lower belly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노래나 운동에서 배 아래쪽을 단단하게 쓰라고 할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in singing or exercise to tell someone to engage the lower belly.

phrases.en: My lower belly has stuck out as I got older.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살이 쪄서 배 아래쪽이 튀어나온 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that the lower belly has gotten bigger from weight gain.

phrases.en: My lower abdomen has been aching sharply since yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배가 아프다'보다 아픈 위치를 구체적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More specific about where it hurts than just 'my stomach hurts'.

explain_en: Use it when you want to be more specific than '배가 아파요' about where it hurts. In singing and exercise you often hear '아랫배에 힘을 주다' (tighten the lower belly).

examples.en: The child is in a lot of pain after the shot.
He suffered for a long time after the breakup.
It looks like the puppy is hurting in its leg.

examples.ko: 친구가 너무 아파해서 병원에 같이 갔어요.
examples.en: My friend was in so much pain that I went to the hospital with them.

examples.ko: 너무 아파하지 마세요, 곧 괜찮아질 거예요.
examples.en: Try not to be so upset; you will be fine soon.

examples.ko: 아파할 때는 옆에서 말없이 있어 주세요.
examples.en: When someone is hurting, stay quietly by their side.

explain: '아프다'는 내 상태이고, '아파하다'는 다른 사람이 아픈 모습을 밖에서 보고 말할 때 써요. '나는 아파요'는 되지만 '나는 아파해요'는 어색해요. 몸뿐 아니라 마음이 아픈 사람에게도 써요.

phrases.en: I took the child who was in pain to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 사람을 꾸며서 아픈 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a person to describe them looking pained.

phrases.en: I felt heartbroken hearing my friend's story.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 아니라 마음이 힘든 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for emotional pain rather than physical pain.

phrases.en: Don't be too hurt, it will get better.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들어하는 사람을 위로할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to comfort someone who is hurting.

explain_en: 아프다 describes your own condition, while 아파하다 is said about someone you observe being in pain. 나는 아파요 works, but 나는 아파해요 sounds odd. It is used for emotional pain as well as physical.

examples.ko: 감기 때문에 알약을 하루에 세 번 먹어요.
examples.en: I take pills three times a day because of a cold.

examples.ko: 이 알약은 너무 커서 삼키기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This pill is so big that it is hard to swallow.
The pill fell on the floor and I could not find it.

examples.ko: 알약 한 알을 물과 같이 먹었어요.
examples.en: I took one pill together with water.

examples.ko: 가루약이 쓰면 알약으로 바꿔 달라고 하세요.
examples.en: If powdered medicine tastes bitter to you, ask for pills instead.
Both pills and powdered medicine should be taken after meals.

explain: 가루로 된 약은 '가루약', 액체로 된 약은 '물약'이라고 해요. 알약은 '먹다'뿐 아니라 '삼키다'와도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I swallow the pill with water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알약은 씹지 않고 넘기기 때문에 '삼키다'와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pills are swallowed whole, so 삼키다 fits well.

phrases.en: I take one pill in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알약은 '알'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pills are counted with 알.

phrases.en: I split the pill in half and take it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약이 크거나 적게 먹어야 할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the pill is large or a smaller dose is needed.
phrases.en_equiv: to split a pill in half

explain_en: Powdered medicine is 가루약 and liquid medicine is 물약. 알약 goes with 먹다 and also often with 삼키다 (to swallow).

examples.ko: 아이가 앞니가 빠져서 웃을 때 귀여워요.
examples.en: The child lost a front tooth, and looks cute when smiling.

examples.ko: 앞니로 사과를 한 입 베어 물었어요.
examples.en: I took a bite of the apple with my front teeth.
I looked in the mirror and brushed my front teeth carefully.
There is red pepper powder stuck on your front tooth.

examples.ko: 앞니는 음식을 자르고 어금니는 잘게 갈아요.
examples.en: Front teeth cut food and molars grind it up finely.
The baby got front teeth and started taking first steps too.

explain: 글자는 '앞니'지만 소리는 [암니]로 들려요. 안쪽의 이는 '어금니'라고 해요. '이를 닦다', '이가 빠지다'처럼 '이'만 써도 되고 '앞니'는 어느 이인지 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling lost a front tooth, so the words come out whistly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이가 빠질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for a tooth falling out.

phrases.en: I brush my front teeth carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이를 닦는 부분을 정해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to name which teeth you brush.

phrases.en: A rabbit has two big front teeth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이는 '개'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Teeth are counted with '개'.

explain_en: It is written 앞니 but sounds like [암니]. The teeth further back are '어금니'. You can just say '이' as in '이를 닦다' or '이가 빠지다', and use 앞니 when you need to say which tooth.

examples.en: I caught a head cold and my nose keeps running.
My head cold is bad, so I can't smell anything.
I get a stuffy-nose cold whenever the seasons change.
My voice sounds strange because of my cold.
A head cold gets better after a few days of rest.
I took cold medicine last night, and now I'm sleepy.

explain: 콧물과 코막힘이 중심인 감기를 말해요. 목이 아픈 감기는 '목감기'라고 해서 증상에 따라 나눠 부르기도 해요. 보통 '코감기에 걸리다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: My head cold got better after taking medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감기가 좋아질 때는 '낫다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'natda' when a cold gets better.

phrases.en: I bought cold medicine for a stuffy nose at the pharmacy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 콧물과 코막힘에 먹는 약을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Medicine for a runny or stuffy nose.

phrases.en: I have a head cold, so I wore a mask.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이다'로 지금 어떤 감기인지 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using 'to be' to say what kind of cold you have.

explain_en: It means a cold whose main symptoms are a runny or blocked nose. A cold with a sore throat is called '목감기', so people sometimes name colds by their symptoms. You usually say '코감기에 걸리다'.

examples.en: Your new perm suits you well.
I got a perm at the hair salon yesterday.
Permed hair looks prettier when you wet it.
I have permed hair, so it's easy to style in the morning.
Since I changed to permed hair, my overall look has changed.

examples.ko: 저기 짧은 파마머리 아주머니가 우리 이모예요.
examples.en: The woman with short permed hair over there is my aunt.

explain: 파마로 만든 곱슬한 머리를 말해요. 타고난 곱슬은 '곱슬머리', 파마를 안 한 곧은 머리는 '생머리'라고 해서 구분해요. 보통 '파마를 하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I got a perm to change my mood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파마하는 일을 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural way to say you got a perm.

phrases.en: My older sister looks good with permed hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리 모양이 잘 맞을 때 '어울리다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use with 어울리다 when a hairstyle suits someone.

phrases.en: I find straight hair more comfortable than permed hair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파마를 안 한 곧은 머리라서 파마머리와 반대예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Straight hair without a perm, the opposite of 파마머리.

explain_en: It means curly hair made with a perm. Naturally curly hair is '곱슬머리' and straight hair without a perm is '생머리'. People usually say '파마를 하다' for getting a perm.

examples.en: In winter you need to wear a parka to stay warm.
The parka has a hood attached.

examples.ko: 이 파카는 가볍고 따뜻해서 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: This parka is light and warm, so I like it.
A friend gave me a parka as a gift.
The parka was too big, so I rolled up the sleeves.
I bought a parka and gloves together.

explain: 모자가 달린 두꺼운 겨울 겉옷이에요. '패딩', '점퍼', '코트'도 겨울에 입는 겉옷이에요.

phrases.en: It was cold, so I took out a thick parka.
phrases.nuance_ko: '두꺼운'을 붙여 겨울 옷의 특징을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '두꺼운' describes the warm, thick feel of the coat.

phrases.en: The room was hot, so I took off my parka.
phrases.nuance_ko: '입다'와 반대로 옷을 벗을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '입다'; use it when taking the coat off.

phrases.en: There are gloves in my parka pocket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷의 일부를 말할 때 '파카'를 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '파카' before a part of the coat to name it.

explain_en: A parka is a thick winter coat with a hood. '패딩', '점퍼' and '코트' are also winter outerwear.

en: to be tired; to be exhausted; to be fatigued

examples.en: I have a lot of work, so my body is tired lately.
I walked all day, so my legs were tired.

examples.ko: 피로한 날에는 일찍 자는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: On tiring days, it is good to sleep early.

examples.ko: 눈이 피로할 땐 먼 곳을 보세요.
examples.en: When your eyes are tired, look at something far away.
I want to cut down on things that wear me out.
You look very tired, so please rest a bit.

explain: '피곤하다'와 비슷하지만 '피로하다'는 더 딱딱해서 글이나 뉴스, 건강 이야기에 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '피곤하다'가 자연스러워요. '피로 회복'처럼 명사 '피로'도 써요.

phrases.en: You look very tired today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 모습을 보고 말할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used when commenting on how someone looks.

phrases.en: I slept enough, so I'm not tired.
phrases.nuance_ko: '피로하다'의 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form of 피로하다.

phrases.en: I'm so tired today that I'll go to bed early.
phrases.nuance_ko: '피로하다'와 뜻이 같고, 일상 대화에서는 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and more natural in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It is close to '피곤하다' but stiffer, so it fits writing, news, and health topics. In daily conversation '피곤하다' sounds more natural. The noun 피로 is used in '피로 회복' (recovery from fatigue).

examples.ko: 하이힐을 신고 오래 걸으면 발이 아파요.
examples.en: If you walk a long time in high heels, your feet hurt.
The new high heels are pretty but uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 면접 때 하이힐 대신 편한 구두를 신었어요.
examples.en: For the interview I wore comfortable shoes instead of high heels.
I wasn't used to high heels and almost fell.
Mom bought me both high heels and sneakers.
Climbing stairs in high heels is hard.

explain: 굽이 높은 구두를 가리켜요. 줄여서 '힐'이라고도 해요. 신는 동작은 '신다'를 써서 '하이힐을 신다'라고 말해요. 굽이 낮고 납작한 신발은 '플랫슈즈'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I wore high heels to work today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발은 '신다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shoes take the verb 신다.

phrases.en: I took off my high heels as soon as I got home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발을 벗는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes taking the shoes off.

phrases.en: I wore heels today, so my feet hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하이힐'을 줄인 말로 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of 하이힐 used in daily talk.

explain_en: It means shoes with high heels, and is shortened to '힐'. Use the verb '신다': '하이힐을 신다'. Low, flat shoes are called '플랫슈즈'.
